errorCodes.meaning: This VTA does not create did:webs DIDs: creation is off while the integration is alpha, and is turned on in its configuration. Existing did:webs DIDs are unaffected.

`didClass` is `service`, and this VTA's configuration does not enable did:webs service DIDs. A service did:webs is optional and alpha (CONVENTIONS.md §1.1), and is enabled separately from did:webs creation. A relationship or persona DID is unaffected.

The DID's class disagrees with the identity it would become or replace: a relationship or persona DID that would be a node's or a service's identity, or a service DID that would replace a persona DID as a context's primary. A DID belongs to one class only (VTI-KEY-193).
The VTA has no hosting server registered under `serverId`.
The hosting server does not host did:webs DIDs: it must run with did:webs hosting (`method-webs`) enabled.
The hosting server serves no such domain, or none for this VTA.
The hosting server refused the slot path: its grammar, a reserved prefix, or a path it does not let this VTA use.
No template of that name is visible in the requested scope, the global scope or the built-ins.
The template's `requiredVars` are not all supplied in `templateVars`, a variable the template does not declare was supplied, or a placeholder stayed unresolved. Nothing was derived.

The template describes a document the did:webs derivation cannot reproduce: a key-role template, a key slot or algorithm the key state cannot hold, a further verification method or relationship, a service or alias the designations cannot carry, or a member the derivation does not render (CONVENTIONS.md §9.2). Nothing was derived; `details` names the rule and the members.
An additional service uses `#didcomm` or `#tsp`, or two services share an id.
The hosting server refused the publication. Nothing was created; `details.hostError` carries what the server said.

DesignatedService.description: A DID document service entry the AID designates for itself: an ACDC it issues in its own registry, anchored in its key event log, which the host renders into `service`. Not a KERI endpoint reply, which can carry only KERI's own roles and URL schemes. `id` is a fragment relative to the DID. Members other than `id`, `type` and `serviceEndpoint` are carried as the DID document data model allows.

id.description: The service's fragment, such as `#files`. `#didcomm` and `#tsp` are the VTA's own (see `addMediatorService` and `addTspService`), and an id a KERI endpoint reply of the AID already establishes cannot be reused.

serviceEndpoint.description: A URI, a map, or a set of either, as the DID document data model allows.

type.description: The service type, matched by peers on its value, never on `id`.

DesignatedService.title: DesignatedService

Ext.description: Vendor-namespaced extension object per SPEC.md §4.5.1. Each immediate key MUST be a reverse-DNS namespace; structure under each namespace is opaque to the framework.

Response.title: VTA did:webs DIDs Create — response payload

WebsDidClass.description: The DID class the DID belongs to (VTI specification, DID classes, VTI-KEY-190 – 193), stated when it is created and fixed for its life. `relationship`: an identifier for one relationship, one community or one trust context, and nothing else. `persona`: a person's own identity. `service`: the durable identity of a node or a service — the VTA itself, a VTC, a VTN, a trust registry, a host service, a mediator, or an integration the VTA provisions — at key assurance level 1. A DID belongs to one class only (VTI-KEY-193): a persona or relationship DID is never adopted as a node's identity, and a service DID is never used as a person's. A service did:webs is alpha: see CONVENTIONS.md §1.
WebsDidClass.title: WebsDidClass

WebsSlotPath.description: The path segments a did:webs DID's slot carries before its AID, separated by `/`: lowercase letters, digits and hyphens. The VTA appends the AID as the final segment, and the hosting server checks that the published stream establishes exactly that AID. `people/alice` on `example.com` gives the slot `people/alice/<AID>` and the DID `did:webs:example.com:people:alice:<AID>`. The caller never writes the AID: it is the digest of an inception event that does not exist until the VTA writes it.
WebsSlotPath.title: WebsSlotPath

schema.description: Create a did:webs DID of a stated DID class — relationship, persona or service — in a context, from explicit members or a DID template: the VTA derives the keys, writes the KERI v2 inception and designation events, and publishes keri.cesr through a hosting server. Level 1. A service did:webs is optional and alpha. Alpha.

addMediatorService.description: Designate a `#didcomm` service, typed `DIDCommMessaging`, whose endpoint is the VTA's mediator's DID. Absent means no. Not with `template`.

addTspService.description: Designate a `#tsp` service, typed `TSPTransport`, whose endpoint is the VTA's mediator's DID. Absent means no. Not with `template`.

additionalServices.description: Further services to designate. None may use `#didcomm` or `#tsp`. Not with `template`.

alsoKnownAs.description: Further DIDs to designate as aliases, such as the subject's did:webvh. The DID itself is always designated, first, and is not listed here. Not with `template`.

contextId.description: Context the DID belongs to. Its keys are derived here, and deleting the context destroys them.

didClass.description: The DID class the new DID is created in, fixed for its life (VTI-KEY-190 – 193). Required: the VTA does not infer a class from a template, a context or a path. `service` makes it the durable identity of a node or a service at level 1, and is refused with `serviceDidNotPermitted` unless the VTA's configuration enables did:webs service DIDs.

domain.description: Hosting domain to publish under, when the server serves more than one. Absent uses the server's default domain. The domain is part of the DID, and is fixed once the DID designates itself.

label.description: Operator-facing label. Recorded for audit, never published.

path.description: Path segments before the AID. Absent puts the AID directly under the domain (`did:webs:<domain>:<AID>`). The VTA appends the AID; the caller never writes it.

serverId.description: The hosting server to publish through: one the VTA has registered (vta/webvh/servers/*), running with did:webs hosting enabled. Required: a did:webs DID is hosted only, since the VTA has no inbound surface to serve one from.

setPrimary.description: Make this the context's primary DID. Refused with `didClassConflict` where the DID's class and the identity it would replace or become disagree (CONVENTIONS.md §1.2).

template.description: DID template to shape the DID from (vta/did-templates/*): its services, aliases and integration kind. The VTA reads the rendered document and designates what the did:webs derivation can express, and refuses with `templateNotRepresentable` a template it cannot (CONVENTIONS.md §9). The keys are always the VTA's. Excludes `addMediatorService`, `addTspService`, `additionalServices` and `alsoKnownAs`.

templateContext.description: Context whose templates to resolve `template` against. Absent uses the global scope, then the built-ins. Only with `template`.

templateVars.description: Variables for the template's placeholders, checked by the VTA's template renderer. Rendered into a published document: never a secret. Only with `template`.
